title: Chapter 8 Revision: Transport & Travel
description: Mixed questions covering motion verbs iść/jechać, do+genitive, genitive singular and plural, and transport vocabulary.

questions.prompt: I'm walking to the market square right now. Which verb is correct?
questions.explanation: 'Idę' = going on foot right now (current motion). 'Jadę' = by vehicle. 'Chodzę' = habitually on foot.

questions.prompt: She regularly commutes to work by train. Which is correct?
questions.explanation: 'Jeździ' (jeździć) = habitual vehicle motion. 'Jedzie' = current trip by vehicle. 'Pociągiem' = by train (instrumental).
'Do + genitive': Gdańsk (m) → Gdańska. 'Jadę do Gdańska' = I'm going to Gdańsk.
'Dworzec' = station (train/bus). 'Idę na dworzec' = I'm going to the station.
'Nie ma + genitive': chleb (m animate) → chleba. 'Nie ma chleba' = There is no bread.

questions.prompt: Nie mam ___ (I don't have a ticket). [bilet → genitive after negation]
questions.explanation: After negation, accusative → genitive: bilet (m inanimate) → biletu. 'Nie mam biletu' = I don't have a ticket.

questions.prompt: W Krakowie jest dużo ___ (In Kraków there are a lot of tourists). [turysta → genitive plural]
questions.explanation: 'Dużo + genitive plural': turysta (m animate) → turystów. Masculine animate genitive plural: -ów.
'Pieszo' = on foot. 'Chodzę do pracy pieszo' = I walk to work.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between 'jestem w domu' and 'idę do domu'?
options: I'm at home vs. I'm going home.
I'm going home vs. I'm at home.
I was home vs. I went home.
I came home vs. I left home.
questions.explanation: 'W domu' = at home (locative, position). 'Do domu' = (going) home (genitive, direction). Essential distinction!

questions.prompt: Kupiłem sześć ___ (I bought six oranges). [pomarańcza → genitive plural]
questions.explanation: After 6 (5+), use genitive plural: pomarańcza (f) → pomarańczy. Feminine genitive plural often has zero ending or -y/-i.
'Wakacje' = holiday / vacation. 'Jadę na wakacje' = I'm going on holiday.
Transport: instrumental case. 'Samochód' → 'samochodem'. 'Jadę samochodem' = I'm going by car.
